title: Bernice Reape's story of adding a middle to 'Prelude to a Kiss'
summary: A visitor tells how she added a bridge to Ellington's tune at his apartment, then heard it on the radio; she now studies harmony.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: It's July the 21st. When I came in, there was a young lady

sitting here with Maxine Sullivan, and they told me the most incredible story which I think we should get on this tape right now.
Do you want to introduce yourself?
(Inaudible) without rehearsing?
Your name.
Bernice Reape.
Okay. That's R-e-a-p-e.
Right.
Okay. And where were you born and in what year?
June 26, 1918, New York City.
When I came in, you were claiming credit for one of the most lovely pieces of music in the history of American -- Afro-American music, I guess. Do you want to tell us about it?
Yes.
This happened many, many years ago. My girlfriend's mother at the time friendly with Duke Ellington. And we were invited to his apartment. While we were at his apartment, they were
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
talking in another room, and I went into the living room.
And in the living room -- he was living at 555 Edgecombe Avenue at that time. In the living room was a gorgeous baby grand piano about the size like that.
And he written some music. And among the pieces he was working on at that time was a piece that was called "Prelude to a Kiss."
So he started the piece, but he hadn't finished the middle. And I sat down, I listened, I thought I liked it -- and the tune was very beautiful.
So (let me see) if I can't put a middle to it just for my own satisfaction. So I sat down and I put, what I thought was the middle to it, and then we left and went home and that was that.
We went back by my friend's mother -- her mother and him broke up and they went back to Chicago.
Do you remember what her name was?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Her name was Tilden. Her father was Dr. Tilden at that time in Chicago. Anyhow, I lost contact with them. So, a few months later, I happened to put the radio on in my house and I heard this piece called 'Prelude to a Kiss.' The minute I heard it, I said, 'Oooooh! That's mine.' And right away (inaudible), I said, 'That's my piece.' I didn't know that my middle was in there. I was surprised too. So then I heard, 'da, la, la, la. Then I heard -- 'Oh, that's mine!' to myself. And that was that. And that's that.

It just goes to show you some of these sections of tunes can show up in some of the most unusual places. Bernice is a friend of mine who is a very good pianist. And right now, we ran into each other at Davidson Senior Center. Bernice is the house pianist for the senior center.
That's why I come over here today. See what happens?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
There wasn't even a hint of Duke Ellington in your (ble) playing. You can do those romantic things --
Right.
Bernice is studying right now. She sits for a long time. She --
I'm going to school right now.
She has studied --
College of New Rochelle.
The College of New Rochelle?
Right.
In the beginning, she was just a pianist and hadn't had theory in how many --
I had no theory! And no harmony. I'm a retiree, so I decided to see the Housing Authority to work with the Housing Authority.
And they have a school for retirees which is free. So I go down to the school and part of the school is giving harmony and theory which is what I want. Although I had played, I never had any

harmony and theory.
So I when I sat down and wrote this music at Ellington's house, I didn't know what I was going. I mean, I couldn't read. And there we have a teacher who's teaching us music harmony and music and theory.
That's good. That's very good.
Well let's hope you can produce a lot more sequences of eight bars of music as lovely as that one in.
Okay.
